subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls, rate limits & routing
messages:
From: Alicia Turner <alicia.turner@acmehealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from call — multi-tenant controls & quotas

Hi Sean / Monica,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good conversation. Wanted to capture the key points from our side so we’re aligned on pain, success criteria, and the immediate asks. I’ve attached our short requirements doc (acme-prod-requirements.pdf).

Pain / background
- We run a single inference cluster that serves multiple customers (B2B SaaS).
- Current issues: noisy tenants causing spikes, no per-tenant quotas, and difficulty routing higher-tier customers to dedicated capacity.
- We need fine-grained billing/observability per customer (token-level accounting + latency SLOs).

What we heard from Redwood on the call
- Support for per-customer rate limits and quotas at the API key/tenant level.
- Ability to route traffic to dedicated pools or cheaper shared pools based on tiering rules.
- Audit logs for routing decisions and token usage.

Success criteria (what will make a pilot successful)
1) Per-tenant rate limits and soft/hard quotas enforced at the gateway.
2) Route high-priority customers to dedicated capacity with predictable latency < 200ms p95 for short requests.
3) Token-level usage exported to our billing system (CSV/JSON).
4) SOC2 evidence + network isolation options for regulated customers.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Can Redwood share an overview doc on multi-tenancy controls and a ballpark for pilot pricing? (we’re budgeted for a pilot in Q2)
- Technical contact for mapping our current API keys and tenant IDs into Redwood routing rules.
- Any constraints on per-tenant TPS / concurrent streams we should be aware of.

Attaching: acme-prod-requirements.pdf (short list of tenants, expected QPS, and compliance notes)

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Turner
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Health
alicia.turner@acmehealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Turner <alicia.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from call — multi-tenant controls & quotas

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear recap and for sending the requirements doc. Putting this in writing as discussed so we have aligned next steps.

Quick recap from Redwood’s side
- We can support per-tenant rate limits and both soft + hard quota enforcement at the request gateway. Limits can be configured per API key or tenant ID, and we provide burst windows for short spikes.
- Routing: policy-based routing allows you to route by tenant metadata to (a) shared low-cost pools, (b) dedicated reserved pools, or (c) region-specific capacity. Fallback rules are available if dedicated capacity is full.
- Billing & telemetry: token-level usage exports (CSV/JSON) and per-tenant dashboards. Audit logs include routing decisions and quota violations.
- Compliance: we can share SOC2 summary and network isolation options; Private deployment available for regulated customers.

Answering your asks
- Overview doc: attaching our multi-tenancy controls overview (redwood-multi-tenant-controls.pdf). Also linking the product doc: https://docs.redwood.com/multi-tenancy-controls
- Pilot pricing: for a small pilot (up to 50 tenants, up to 200 TPS aggregate) we typically propose a 3-month pilot with a reserved pool + usage-based add-on — I’ll put a ballpark in the HubSpot deal and share formal quote after mapping traffic.
- Technical contact: looping in Neha (cc’d) from our Applied ML / infra team to map tenant IDs and discuss routing rule templates.

Proposed next steps
1) Tech sync (30-45m) this week — Neha to cover routing rule templates and quota enforcement semantics.
2) Provide sample mapping: we’ll send a short JSON schema for tenant metadata and API key mapping.
3) Pilot proposal + ballpark pricing in HubSpot.

If that plan looks good, I’ll schedule the tech sync for Wed or Thu.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Hi Alicia — glad we had the intro today. Adding a few technical clarifications from the infra side so you have concrete constraints and options ahead of the tech sync.

Technical notes
- Rate limits / quotas
  * Enforced at the gateway per API key / tenant_id. Support token-bucket soft limits + hard cutoffs.
  * Configurable windows: per-second, per-minute, per-hour. We can also support SLA prioritization (e.g., paid-tier tokens bypass soft-limits until sustained breach).
- Tiering & routing
  * Routing policies are label-based. You can attach a routing_label to tenants (e.g., tier:gold, region:us-west).
  * Policy examples: route tier:gold -> dedicated-pool-us-west; tier:silver -> shared-pool-high-performance; fallback -> shared-pool-economy.
  * When dedicated pools are at capacity, automatic fallback + optional queueing (max wait time) are available.
- Observability / billing
  * Per-tenant token export (JSON or CSV). We can also push to an S3 bucket or a BigQuery sink.
  * Tracing: per-request headers preserved to map requests back to tenant IDs.
- Constraints we need from your side prior to the tech sync
  1) Expected TPS per tenant and a 95th percentile request size (tokens) for the top 10 tenants.
  2) Number of tenants you want in the initial pilot (suggest 25-50).
  3) Any regulatory customers that must be on Private deployment (SOC2 + network isolation).

Attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC2 summary & audit coverage)

I’ll prepare a short template for the tenant -> API key mapping and share before the sync. Wed/Thu both work for me; Sean if you confirm I’ll book.

Thanks — Neha
